newsitem.title: OMAN: Syrian leaders in Oman for talks with Sultan.
newsitem.headline: Syrian leaders in Oman for talks with Sultan.

text.p: Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam arrived in Muscat on Wednesday for talks with Sultan Qaboos bin Said as part of a regional tour, the official Omani News Agency (ONA) said.
Khaddam, accompanied by Foreign Minister Farouq al-Shara, would hand the sultan a letter from Syrian President Hafez al-Assad, it added but gave no further details.

They arrived from Abu Dhabi, capital of the United Arab Emirates (UAE), where Khaddam brushed aside Israeli suggestions their bilateral Middle East peace talks are about to resume after a 10-month break.
They have also been to Saudi Arabia and Kuwait.
"There is no movement until now regarding resumption of talks on the Syrian and Lebanese tracks," he said after talks with UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan late on Tuesday.
"The Israeli media campaign expressing optimism regarding restarting talks aims at misleading public opinion," he added in remarks carried by the UAE official WAM news agency.

Both Syrian officials are touring the area to drum up support for Syria's peace stand after Israel and the PLO settled their deadlock on the West Bank town of Hebron earlier this month, Gulf Arab newspapers have said.
Syria, they said, does not want Arab countries to pressure it to restart talks with Israel because of the recent deal.
"He (Khaddam) denied that any pressure was being exerted on Syria to jump start the talks and said Syria would not bow to any pressure when the matter dealt with its land and pride," WAM said.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday that the United States was trying to find a "bridging formula" to get both states to revive their talks.
Netanyahu and other Israeli officials have said there were contacts with Syria through the United States, the main sponsor of the five-year-old process and other channels.
Syria demands the return of the Golan Heights, captured by Israel in 1967. Israel broke off talks with Syria after a series of Islamist suicide bombings in Israel last February and March.
